hops.title: Compare it: petals have marks like runway lights
hops.text: Runway lights help a pilot find the runway. Petals can help bees in a similar way. Many flowers that bees visit have an ultraviolet pattern around the flower's centre that bees can see and we can't. Tell your child these petals carry secret marks guiding bees toward the flower's centre, where the nectar is.

image.alt: AI-generated illustration: A fuzzy bumblebee hovering over a plain bright yellow wildflower in a sunny garden.
image.caption: Many flowers that bees visit carry ultraviolet marks around the centre that we cannot see, guiding bees to the middle.

hops.title: Say it: bumblebees buzz pollen loose
hops.text: While your child dabs the swab from cup to cup, try saying, "A bumblebee can grab some flowers and buzz its flight muscles, shaking the pollen loose like a pepper shaker." It is true: the United States and Canada have about 46 native kinds of bumblebee, and on some flowers they grip with their jaws and buzz the pollen out.

sources.citation: U.S. National Park Service, Pollinators: Bumble bee

image.alt: AI-generated illustration: A plump bumblebee clinging to a yellow flower while a small cloud of pollen shakes loose.
image.caption: On some flowers, a bumblebee holds on and buzzes its flight muscles to shake the pollen loose.

hops.afterHeading: Questions to ask while you do it
hops.title: Ask it: what colour helps a flower get found at night?
hops.text: While you look at the bright petals, ask, "If a flower only opened after bedtime, what colour would help a moth spot it?" Welcome any guess, even black or glow-in-the-dark. Then share that many night flowers are white or pale, so they stand out after sunset, with a strong scent that moths, such as hawkmoths, can follow upwind.

sources.citation: USDA Forest Service, Plant Strategies: Visual Cues

image.alt: AI-generated illustration: A hawkmoth hovering in front of a white night-blooming flower beneath a twilight sky.
image.caption: Pale petals and a strong evening scent help moths find flowers that open at night.
